dossier.purpose: CodeGraph (npm @colbymchenry/codegraph) is a local-first code-intelligence library, CLI and stdio MCP server. It parses a repo with tree-sitter (native Rust kernel for 20 language ids, WASM grammars for the rest), stores symbols/edges/files in a per-project SQLite+FTS5 DB (.codegraph/codegraph.db), resolves cross-file references with import, name-matching and framework heuristics, and returns verbatim symbol source plus call paths and a blast-radius summary to coding agents. It is a structural graph index, not a language-server client: the code has no LSP client, no edit/rename tool and no post-edit diagnostics (src/mcp/tools.ts:1552-1568; src/mcp/server-instructions.ts:72-77; AGENTS.md:9).

claims.claim: CodeGraph hands the agent the exact code it needs in one call: a pre-built graph of every symbol, call edge and dependency, returning relevant source, call paths (incl. dynamic-dispatch hops) and blast radius.
As an MCP server it exposes a single tool, codegraph_explore; node/search/callers/callees/impact/files/status stay functional but unlisted unless CODEGRAPH_MCP_TOOLS re-enables them.
codegraph_explore returns the relevant symbols' verbatim source grouped by file plus call paths and a blast-radius summary; naming a file or symbol returns its current line-numbered source like Read.

Extraction runs in a native Rust kernel with compiled-in tree-sitter grammars for 20 languages (others and per-file fallbacks use the portable engine), stored in local SQLite+FTS5, then references are resolved (calls, imports, inheritance, framework patterns).
Impact analysis: trace callers, callees and impact radius of a symbol; CLI has callers, callees, impact, affected, query, node, files.
Auto-sync is on by default via a native-event watcher ('The index is never stale'), 2000ms default debounce, a per-file staleness banner, and connect-time catch-up.

codegraph install auto-configures Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI, opencode, Hermes, Gemini CLI, Antigravity, Kiro and GitHub Copilot: MCP server config, a marker-fenced section in CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md/GEMINI.md, and Claude auto-allow permissions; it does not index code.
Manual Claude Code setup: mcpServers.codegraph stdio entry (codegraph serve --mcp, alwaysLoad true) in ~/.claude.json, optional allow of mcp__codegraph__* in ~/.claude/settings.json.
Supported Agents section says the MCP server delivers its own guidance 'so no instructions file is written'.
Every listed language gets 'full structural extraction and cross-file resolution'; Objective-C is 'Partial support'.
Measured cross-file 'fair coverage' per language on one benchmark repo each (TS/JS 95.8%, Python 100%, Go 96.6%, Rust 86.7%, Java 93.3%, C# 85.2%, Liquid 73.8%); framework routing 74-100%.

'100% Local - No data leaves your machine. No API keys. No external services.' while a separate section says anonymous usage statistics are collected (off via codegraph telemetry off, CODEGRAPH_TELEMETRY=0 or DO_NOT_TRACK=1).
Every release ships a self-contained build (bundled Node runtime) for Windows, macOS and Linux on x64 and arm64.

Releases are built by the public Release workflow; npm uses OIDC trusted publishing with provenance; GitHub Release bundles and SHA256SUMS carry signed attestations (SLSA v1.0 Build Level 2); pre-July-2026 releases have none.

install.method: Wire agents (required after CLI install; does not index)

platforms.linux_x86_64: yes - README.md:786 (Linux x64/arm64 via shell installer or npm); install.sh:44-49 maps x86_64 to linux-x64; release.yml:49-50 builds the linux-x64 kernel on ubuntu-22.04 and release.yml:199 the linux-x64 bundle (bundled Node v24.16.0, scripts/build-bundle.sh:24). No musl/Alpine target is listed (scripts/build-bundle.sh:13-15). No CI job runs the full test suite on Linux. The only automated tests are the 17 __tests__/kernel-*.test.ts contract/parity suites, run on ubuntu-latest against the linux-x64 kernel by the manually dispatched release workflow (release.yml:23-24,72,179-195). Full-suite Linux validation is manual via Docker (AGENTS.md:192-198).
platforms.wsl2: yes, with documented caveats - no WSL2 row in README.md:782-786; WSL2 appears only in Troubleshooting. On /mnt/<drive> projects the shared-daemon socket is unreliable (falls back to in-process serving or CODEGRAPH_NO_DAEMON=1, README.md:891), SQLite WAL may not enable (README.md:882-886), and WSL keeps its own .codegraph-wsl index separate from Windows (README.md:895; src/db/wsl-shared-index.ts:1-15; src/directory.ts:20,97-101). serve --no-watch exists for slow /mnt drives (src/bin/codegraph.ts:2158). No WSL2 CI.
platforms.macos_arm64: yes - README.md:785 (macOS x64/arm64); install.sh:34-48 maps Darwin/arm64 to darwin-arm64; release.yml:47-48 builds the aarch64-apple-darwin kernel on macos-14 and release.yml:199 the darwin-arm64 bundle. Maintainer dev machine and default test target is macOS (AGENTS.md:190), but the 2026-09 audit says macOS was unavailable for its runs (docs/benchmarks/regression-audit-2026-09.md:99-100,216-217). Bundles are not notarized (BUNDLING.md:67-70).
platforms.gpu: no - not applicable. No GPU, embedding or ML-inference code or dependency found; src/mcp/tools.ts:3877 says ranking is 'deterministic, no embeddings'; runtime deps are listed in package.json:44-55 and codegraph-kernel/Cargo.toml:12-63. Work runs on CPU (Rust kernel + worker threads).

integrations.cli: yes - 'codegraph' (commander): install, uninstall, init, uninit, index, sync, status, unlock, query, explore, context, node, files, callers, callees, impact, affected, daemon, telemetry, upgrade, version (README.md:526-549; src/bin/codegraph.ts:789-2879). Hidden: serve, prompt-hook. ui/web refused unless CODEGRAPH_UI=1 (src/bin/viewer-gate.ts:5-11). No CLI command edits source files.
integrations.mcp: yes - stdio server 'codegraph serve --mcp' (src/bin/codegraph.ts:2154-2189), runs direct, via proxy, or as a detached per-project daemon over a Unix socket/named pipe (src/mcp/index.ts:17-35; src/mcp/daemon.ts:249-251). Default listed tool: codegraph_explore only (src/mcp/tools.ts:1850); eight tools are defined (search, callers, callees, impact, node, explore, status, files; tools.ts:1581-1759) and all carry readOnlyHint true (tools.ts:1552-1568). No tool performs symbol-level edits, renames or diagnostics, and none queries a language server. Capabilities advertised: tools only (src/mcp/session.ts:252-257).
integrations.sdk_or_api: Library: yes - package exports the CodeGraph class (init/open/indexAll/sync/searchNodes/getCallers/getCallees/getImpactRadius/buildContext/watch) (README.md:595-636; package.json:9-10; src/index.ts:489-2360); needs Node 22.5+ for node:sqlite (README.md:632-634). HTTP API: none for the product; a read-only JSON API exists only inside the gated codegraph ui viewer bound to 127.0.0.1 (src/ui-server/index.ts:451; src/ui-server/constants.ts:21; AGENTS.md:91-92).
integrations.claude_code_or_codex: Claude Code: MCP entry in ~/.claude.json (user) or ./.mcp.json (project) with alwaysLoad true, allow-rule mcp__codegraph__* in settings.json, a marker-fenced CodeGraph block in CLAUDE.md, and an opt-in default-yes UserPromptSubmit hook running 'codegraph prompt-hook' that injects codegraph_explore output on how/where/trace prompts (src/installer/targets/claude.ts:124-172,457-498; src/installer/index.ts:208-231; src/bin/codegraph.ts:1455-1609). The hook is not mentioned in README.md. No LSP wiring, no PostToolUse/diagnostics hook and no Claude Code plugin manifest found; pre-0.8 PostToolUse mark-dirty hooks are only stripped (claude.ts:305-323). .claude/skills in the repo are contributor dev skills, not shipped (package.json:14-18). Codex CLI: [mcp_servers.codegraph] in $CODEX_HOME/config.toml or ~/.codex plus a marker block in AGENTS.md; local installs apply only in trusted projects (src/installer/targets/codex.ts:1-30,115-126).

readme.telemetry_and_network: Telemetry is default-ON (precedence DO_NOT_TRACK > CODEGRAPH_TELEMETRY > stored choice > default on: src/telemetry/index.ts:183-206). Daily-aggregated anonymous events (install, index, usage_rollup, uninstall; random machine UUID, version, OS/arch, Node major, CI flag, language names, coarse file-count buckets, tool/command names, MCP client name/version) POST to https://telemetry.getcodegraph.com/v1/events (src/telemetry/index.ts:30; TELEMETRY.md:43-71,99-107), stored in Cloudflare D1 for 90 days (TELEMETRY.md:111-125); ingest source in telemetry-worker/. A first-run stderr notice is printed (src/telemetry/index.ts:396-418); the installer asks, default yes (src/installer/index.ts:185-206). Opt out: codegraph telemetry off, CODEGRAPH_TELEMETRY=0, DO_NOT_TRACK=1 (README.md:741-745). Separately the MCP server checks GitHub for a newer release at most daily (off via CODEGRAPH_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1 or DO_NOT_TRACK; TELEMETRY.md:38-41; src/upgrade/update-check.ts:19-28,89-91; src/upgrade/index.ts:238-259). The interactive installer/upgrade can offer an opt-in email waitlist submit to https://getcodegraph.com/api/waitlist, never under --yes (src/installer/beta-signup.ts:19,80-96,125-169; installer/index.ts:271-280). install.sh and codegraph upgrade download from GitHub Releases (install.sh:60-76; src/upgrade/index.ts:541-565). No accounts, API keys or LLM calls found; indexing and queries are local SQLite. Viewer binds 127.0.0.1 only (src/ui-server/index.ts:451). README.md:284 says 'No external services', which the code qualifies (see claim_checks).

code.architecture: Pipeline: file discovery/watching (src/sync/watcher.ts, src/extraction/index.ts honoring .gitignore and codegraph.json) -> extraction: native Rust kernel (codegraph-kernel/src/*.rs, routed per language by DEFAULT_ROUTED in src/extraction/kernel/index.ts:37-113, per-file fallback to web-tree-sitter WASM on parse errors, kill switch CODEGRAPH_KERNEL=0) plus per-language extractors in src/extraction/languages/ and standalone Svelte/Vue/Astro/Liquid/Razor/MyBatis/DFM/CFML extractors, 29 vendored .wasm grammars in src/extraction/wasm/ -> SQLite via node:sqlite with WAL and FTS5 (src/db/) -> ReferenceResolver (src/resolution/index.ts: import-resolver, name-matcher with a 'fuzzy' strategy and 0-1 confidence per src/resolution/types.ts:42-45, ~30 framework/router modules in src/resolution/frameworks/, whole-graph synthesizers such as callback-synthesizer.ts and tier-synthesizer.ts emitting provenance 'heuristic' edges) -> graph queries (src/graph/traversal.ts callers/callees/impact; named-symbol-flow.ts) -> ContextBuilder (src/context/) -> MCP tools (src/mcp/tools.ts, >7,800 lines; session.ts, engine.ts, query-pool.ts workers) and CLI. Source text is read from disk at query time behind path-containment checks (src/utils.ts:101-163). Installer targets in src/installer/targets/ (antigravity, claude, codex, copilot-cli, copilot-jetbrains, copilot-vscode, cursor, gemini, hermes, kiro, opencode). Gated browser viewer in ui/ + src/ui-server/. Telemetry client src/telemetry/, ingest worker telemetry-worker/. Edge.provenance enum includes 'scip' (src/types.ts:227; src/extraction/kernel/layout.ts:112) but no SCIP/LSP ingestion code was found.
code.packaging_and_release: Artifacts: six self-contained bundles codegraph-{darwin-arm64,darwin-x64,linux-x64,linux-arm64,win32-x64,win32-arm64} (.tar.gz Unix, .zip Windows) holding an official Node runtime (default v24.16.0, downloaded from nodejs.org at build time with no checksum check: scripts/build-bundle.sh:24,36-56), compiled app + prod deps (npm ci --omit=dev --ignore-scripts: :77) and the Rust kernel .node when a prebuild exists (:80-98). .github/workflows/release.yml is manual (workflow_dispatch, :23-24): builds kernel prebuilds on macos-14, ubuntu-22.04, ubuntu-22.04-arm, windows-latest (:42-69), runs only __tests__/kernel-*.test.ts on linux-x64 (:179-195), builds all bundles (:197-202), writes SHA256SUMS (:204-209), attests bundles + SHA256SUMS with actions/attest-build-provenance@v4 (:211-221), creates the GitHub Release (:237-247) and publishes the npm shim plus per-platform optionalDependency packages via OIDC trusted publishing with --provenance (:18-22,249-271). install.sh extracts the downloaded tarball without verifying SHA256SUMS or attestations (install.sh:72-82); the npm shim verifies SHA256SUMS only on its self-heal fallback download and skips when absent (scripts/npm-shim.js:203-228). No macOS notarization/Windows Authenticode; Homebrew/Scoop are TODO (BUNDLING.md:58,67-70). BUNDLING.md:65 and AGENTS.md:268 still say NPM_TOKEN is required, contradicting the workflow. Latest release 1.6.1 dated 2026-09-29 (CHANGELOG.md:16).
code.tests_and_ci: Vitest ^2.1.9, two projects: engine (node) and ui (jsdom) (vitest.config.mts:10-14; vitest.workspace.mts:27-62). About 318 *.test.ts files under __tests__/ (315 top-level + 3 in __tests__/integration/), plus __tests__/evaluation/ run by npm run eval and not part of npm test (AGENTS.md:178), and 29 #[test]/#[cfg(test)] hits in 7 Rust files of codegraph-kernel. Tests use real SQLite and temp dirs with no DB mocking (AGENTS.md:182). CI: .github/workflows has only release.yml (manual; runs just the kernel parity tests before packaging) and deploy-site.yml (Astro docs deploy on push to main touching site/**). No workflow runs npm test on pushes or pull requests; cross-platform validation is manual (macOS local, Linux via Docker, Windows via a VM; AGENTS.md:190-214). The repo's 2026-09 audit reports the monolithic extraction suite's worker is SIGKILLed near 1.6-1.7 GB RSS, 'no claim of a full green monolithic suite', and reviewer-reported 4,636 pass/3 fail vs 4,600/18 before repairs (docs/benchmarks/regression-audit-2026-09.md:66-75,87-93).
code.dependencies: Root package.json: 10 runtime deps (@clack/prompts, commander, fast-string-width, fast-wrap-ansi, ignore, jsonc-parser, picomatch, sisteransi, tree-sitter-wasms, web-tree-sitter) and 7 devDeps; workspace 'ui' (package.json:19-21,44-64). ui/package.json (private): 1 dep (@xyflow/svelte), 1 peer (svelte), 8 dev. site/package.json: 5 deps. telemetry-worker/package.json: 0 deps, 2 dev. telemetry-dashboard/package.json: 0 deps, 3 dev. codegraph-kernel/Cargo.toml: 20 [dependencies] (napi, napi-derive, tree-sitter 0.25, sha2, regex, 14 tree-sitter-* grammar crates, tree-sitter-language) + libc on unix + 2 build-deps (napi-build, cc); vendored C grammars for kotlin/lua/scala/dart; 29 prebuilt grammar .wasm files committed in src/extraction/wasm/. code.security_policy: none - no SECURITY.md, CONTRIBUTING or CODEOWNERS in the repo; only GitHub issues are linked (README.md:909). In-code measures: refusal of sensitive system/home dirs as roots (src/utils.ts:43-47,175-204), symlink-aware containment for content-serving reads (src/utils.ts:101-163), config-file values never returned (src/utils.ts:55-66), viewer loopback/Host checks (src/ui-server/security.ts:8-44), read-only tool annotations (src/mcp/tools.ts:1552-1568).

claim_checks.claim: MCP exposes a single tool, codegraph_explore (README.md:583)
claim_checks.evidence: DEFAULT_MCP_TOOLS = new Set(['explore']) (src/mcp/tools.ts:1850); getTools() lists only it unless CODEGRAPH_MCP_TOOLS is set (tools.ts:2083-2110; getStaticTools 1830-1837). Eight tools are defined (tools.ts:1581-1759). With no allowlist the de-listed tools stay callable (isToolAllowed returns true, tools.ts:2092-2095); with an allowlist, other calls return 'disabled via CODEGRAPH_MCP_TOOLS' (tools.ts:2665-2668). Stale comment at tools.ts:2105 still says 'default 4-tool surface'.

claim_checks.claim: README positions CodeGraph as a tree-sitter graph served over MCP and makes no language-server, symbol-edit or post-edit-diagnostics claim (README.md:514-520, 583-591); 'Semantic Code Intelligence' appears at README.md:9
claim_checks.evidence: Code agrees: no LSP client in src/ (searches for language server, textDocument/, pyright, tsserver, gopls, clangd hit only comments and the LSP-style rootUri parameter at src/mcp/session.ts:220-231). All eight MCP tools carry readOnlyHint true and none writes to the workspace (src/mcp/tools.ts:1552-1568); the only fs writes under src/mcp are lock/pid/registry files and an opt-in CODEGRAPH_EXPLORE_DEBUG log (src/mcp/explore-diagnostics.ts:11-32). Server instructions say 'No live correctness validation - that's still the TypeScript compiler / test suite / linter's job' (src/mcp/server-instructions.ts:77) and matching is lexical, not by meaning (server-instructions.ts:60); ranking uses graph random-walk, 'no embeddings' (tools.ts:3868-3882). 'scip' exists only as a reserved provenance enum value (src/types.ts:227; src/extraction/kernel/layout.ts:112).

claim_checks.claim: CodeGraph hands the agent the exact code it needs in one call, with call paths and blast radius (README.md:192, 587)
claim_checks.evidence: Symbol source is read from disk at query time behind path-containment checks (src/mcp/tools.ts:5496-5504,7804-7806; src/utils.ts:128-163) and symbol extents come from tree-sitter nodes (src/types.ts:133-162), so definition text is exact. Reference/call edges are inferred: resolver strategies include 'fuzzy' with 0-1 confidence (src/resolution/types.ts:42-45), synthesized hops are provenance 'heuristic' (AGENTS.md:159; src/types.ts:227), and server instructions admit 'Cross-file resolution is best-effort name matching; ambiguous calls may return multiple candidates' (src/mcp/server-instructions.ts:76). Output is size-capped, with truncation declared in the answer (CHANGELOG.md:66,125). Callers/impact traverse calls, references, imports, instantiates and navigates edges (src/graph/traversal.ts:311).

claim_checks.claim: Auto-sync keeps the index current: 'The index is never stale' (README.md:127)
claim_checks.evidence: Watcher debounce defaults to 2000ms with a 300ms quick window for at most 2 pending files (src/sync/watcher.ts:72-73,382,954-967; env clamp 100ms-60s at src/mcp/engine.ts:444-463). Responses carry a staleness banner for pending files and 'auto-sync DISABLED/RECOVERING' banners (src/mcp/tools.ts:1413,1451,1461); server instructions say 'Index lags file writes by ~1 second' (src/mcp/server-instructions.ts:75). README.md:305-307 itself says manual sync is needed when the watcher is disabled (serve --no-watch, CODEGRAPH_NO_DAEMON, WSL /mnt).

claim_checks.claim: '100% Local - No data leaves your machine. No API keys. No external services.' (README.md:284)
claim_checks.evidence: Indexing and querying are local (SQLite; no network in extraction). But anonymous telemetry is default-on and POSTs to telemetry.getcodegraph.com (src/telemetry/index.ts:30,205), the MCP server polls GitHub daily for updates (src/upgrade/update-check.ts:19-28), and the installer can send an email to getcodegraph.com if the user opts in (src/installer/beta-signup.ts:19,86). README.md:733-748 and TELEMETRY.md document telemetry separately.

risks: Scope: not a language-server tool. References are tree-sitter plus name-matching with a 'fuzzy' strategy and 'heuristic' synthesized edges, and the project says cross-file resolution is best-effort and ambiguous calls may return multiple candidates (src/resolution/types.ts:45; src/types.ts:227; src/mcp/server-instructions.ts:76). All MCP tools are read-only; there are no symbol-level edits, renames, LSP navigation or post-edit diagnostics (src/mcp/tools.ts:1552-1568; server-instructions.ts:77).

Trust and context footprint: agent guidance tells the model not to re-verify with grep and to treat returned source as already read (src/mcp/server-instructions.ts:64-66), yet the index can lag edits by the 2s debounce (src/sync/watcher.ts:382) and bounded answers can be truncated (CHANGELOG.md:125). The README admits about 80% more resident retrieval context than a file-reading agent (README.md:198).

Privacy/network: telemetry is default-on (src/telemetry/index.ts:205) and POSTs to telemetry.getcodegraph.com; a daily GitHub update check runs from the MCP server (src/upgrade/update-check.ts:19-28); the installer can submit an email to getcodegraph.com on opt-in (src/installer/beta-signup.ts:19). README.md:284 'No external services' is therefore only true of indexing and querying. Opt-outs exist (DO_NOT_TRACK=1, CODEGRAPH_TELEMETRY=0, CODEGRAPH_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1).

Installer footprint: edits ~/.claude.json or ./.mcp.json, settings.json (allow mcp__codegraph__*), CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md, and adds a Claude Code UserPromptSubmit hook that runs codegraph on prompts, a hook the README never mentions (src/installer/targets/claude.ts:124-172,457-498; src/installer/index.ts:208-231). It may also install git post-commit/merge/checkout hooks when the watcher is off (src/installer/index.ts:654-722). Per-project detached daemons outlive sessions until idle (src/mcp/index.ts:22-30). codegraph uninstall reverses agent configs (README.md:133-139).

Supply chain: install.sh performs no checksum or attestation verification (install.sh:72-82); the bundled Node runtime is downloaded without checksum (scripts/build-bundle.sh:36-56); no notarization/Authenticode (BUNDLING.md:67-70); 29 prebuilt grammar .wasm blobs are committed (src/extraction/wasm/); 1 MB source-file cap and vendored C grammars add review surface. Release is a manual workflow_dispatch run with an admin-owned PAT (release.yml:23-24,77-92); BUNDLING.md:65 and AGENTS.md:268 still cite an NPM_TOKEN the workflow does not use.

Maintenance/QA: no PR or push CI runs the test suite (only release.yml, which runs just kernel parity tests, and deploy-site.yml: release.yml:179-195). The repo's own 2026-09 audit found five correctness regressions in release 1.6.0 and a monolithic-suite worker killed near 1.6-1.7 GB RSS with no full-green claim; macOS was unavailable for it (docs/benchmarks/regression-audit-2026-09.md:12-24,66-75,99-100). No SECURITY.md. Copyright is held by one individual (LICENSE:3).

Platform/runtime limits: Node engines >=20 <25 with a hard exit on 25+ (package.json:65-67; AGENTS.md:58) while node:sqlite needs 22.5+ for library use (README.md:632); WSL2 /mnt projects have unreliable daemon sockets and cannot share a Windows index (README.md:891,895); network/9p filesystems may lack WAL (README.md:882-886); very large repos can grow the WAL up to a 2 GB soft threshold (README.md:897); Objective-C is only partial (README.md:822); 14 of the supported languages (ArkTS, Vue, Svelte, Astro, Liquid, Pascal, ObjC, CFML, COBOL, VB.NET, Erlang, Solidity, Terraform, Nix) run on the WASM path, not the kernel (src/extraction/kernel/index.ts:37-113).

Roadmap/licensing scope: repo is MIT, but a hosted 'CodeGraph platform' and a 'CodeGraph Pro' app are teased (README.md:42-46; src/installer/beta-signup.ts:1-12; AGENTS.md:42-48 says the Pro app imports the private ui package); the browser viewer is gated off by default and 'not released yet' (src/bin/viewer-gate.ts:5-11; AGENTS.md:92).
